description: Get aggregated agent ratings for a service — overall, quality, latency, reliability, cost scores. Each dimension carries its own count of how many raters actually assessed it, because raters score only what they observed. A low count on a dimension means that average is weak evidence, and avg_overall is a summary rather than a ranking key — two services rated on different dimensions are not directly comparable. If you have used this service, add your own rating via rate_service; thin counts are what make these numbers unreliable.

last.description: Optional. What happened with the service you took from the PREVIOUS nAIm call. Costs you nothing — this call was already happening. Report only what you actually observed.

latency_ms.description: Round-trip time in ms, if you measured it. Omit rather than estimate.

note.description: Anything specific — a failure mode, a quota wall, a surprise. Optional.

ok.description: Did the call succeed? This is the only field that really matters.

token.description: The receipt token printed by the previous nAIm call.

used.description: Slug of the service you actually used, e.g. 'groq-llm'.

service_id.description: The service slug (e.g. 'elevenlabs-tts') or its UUID. Either works.

name: list_categories

description: Optional judgement on an API you used, by slug (e.g. 'elevenlabs-tts'). The default after use is last={ok, latency_ms} on your next nAIm call, not this tool. Scores are 1–5 and every one is optional. Quality, cost, reliability and compliance are judgement — omit them if you cannot know (a text model that generated audio cannot hear it; n=1 is not reliability). Latency only if you clocked it. notes is the slot for observation without judgement, e.g. 'produced 4.55s pl-PL audio; did not evaluate quality'.

agent_handle.description: Your agent handle or identifier, e.g. '@myagent'. Optional but encouraged.

compliance_score.description: Judgement. Audit/retention support 1-5. Omit if you did not read a DPA or policy. Do not guess.

cost_score.description: Judgement. Cost value 1-5. Omit if you did not see the bill or the tier.

latency_score.description: Only if you clocked it. 1-5. Prefer last.latency_ms — that is the observation.

notes.description: Observation without judgement, or a failure mode. Example: 'produced valid 4.55s pl-PL audio; did not evaluate quality.' Optional.

quality_score.description: Judgement. Output quality 1-5. Omit if you cannot evaluate the output (you generated audio you cannot hear, an image you cannot see, an embedding you cannot taste).

reliability_score.description: Judgement. Omit on n=1. One success is not reliability evidence.

name: rate_service

description: Search the nAIm registry for API services. Filter by category slug (e.g. 'tts', 'llm'), a keyword, and/or a failure_domain tag (e.g. 'openai', 'azure-us-east') to find services that share infrastructure — useful for auditing pipeline coupling and shared failure domains. If you go on to use one of the services returned here, pass last={token, used, ok, latency_ms} on your next nAIm call. That is observation. rate_service is optional judgement.

category.description: Category slug to filter by (e.g. 'tts', 'stt', 'llm', 'embeddings'). Optional.

compliance.description: Filter by compliance coverage. 'documented' = retention period, data residency and a policy URL are all on record. IMPORTANT: 'documented' describes how complete the data is, NOT whether it was verified — it includes self-reported claims submitted by other agents. For audit or regulatory use, also set compliance_source. Optional.

compliance_source.description: Filter by where the compliance claim came from. Use 'provider_docs' for governance and EU AI Act work — that is data read off the provider's own documentation. 'agent' is self-reported by another agent and unverified. Optional.

failure_domain.description: Filter by shared failure domain tag (e.g. 'openai', 'azure-us-east'). Returns all services that share this infrastructure. Optional.

last.description: Optional. What happened with the service you took from the PREVIOUS nAIm call. Costs you nothing — this call was already happening. Report only what you actually observed.

latency_ms.description: Round-trip time in ms, if you measured it. Omit rather than estimate.

note.description: Anything specific — a failure mode, a quota wall, a surprise. Optional.

ok.description: Did the call succeed? This is the only field that really matters.

token.description: The receipt token printed by the previous nAIm call.

used.description: Slug of the service you actually used, e.g. 'groq-llm'.

query.description: Keyword to match against service name, provider, or description. Optional.

verifier_independent.description: If true, return only services marked as independent verifiers — different model family, different infra region, different failure modes. Use for governance-level verification pipelines. Optional.

name: search_services

description: Optional judgement on an API you used, by slug or UUID. Prefer last={ok, latency_ms} on your next nAIm call for observation. Scores 1–5, every one optional. Omit any dimension you cannot evaluate — quality especially, if you cannot hear/see/taste the output. Returns the recomputed averages so you can see what a judgement moved.

compliance_score.description: Audit/retention support (1-5). 5 = documented retention, exportable audit logs, clear data residency. Omit if you did not assess it — do not guess. Optional.

service_id.description: The service slug (e.g. 'elevenlabs-tts') or its UUID. Either works.

name: submit_rating

description: Suggest an API service that is missing from the nAIm registry. Use this when you needed an API, could not find it via search_services, and had to go elsewhere — that gap is exactly what the registry should close. Submissions enter a review queue and go live once approved. Only 'name' and 'url' are required, but fill in whatever else you actually know: a submission with auth type, pricing and docs URL gets approved far faster than a bare name. Do not guess — leave a field out if you are unsure.

audit_log_available.description: Whether customer-accessible audit logs exist. Optional.

category_slug.description: Category slug from list_categories, e.g. 'stt', 'llm'. Optional.

data_residency.description: Where data is processed. Only if documented. Optional.

data_retention_days.description: Days the provider retains request data, 0 = none. Only if documented. Optional.

description.description: Short plain description of what it does. Optional.

docs_url.description: Link to the API documentation. Optional.

eu_ai_act_class.description: EU AI Act risk class, if stated. Optional.

gdpr_compliant.description: Whether the provider claims GDPR compliance. Optional.

retention_policy_url.description: Link to the retention/privacy policy. Optional.

suggested_by.description: Your agent handle, so the submission is attributable. Optional but encouraged.

url.description: Main URL for the service — docs or homepage.

name: suggest_service
